subject: PrivDeploy capacity ask: rack power, thermal limits, and egress shaping for dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@acme-manufacturing.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: infra@acme-manufacturing.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private pool sizing question — rack power & egress constraints

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving from discovery to sizing for a Private deployment in our Boston colo and need to align on three constraints that will materially change the capacity plan:

1) Power & PDU headroom: our cages are limited to 20kW per rack with a hard PDU limit at 22kW during brief bursts. We need to understand realistic GPU pod counts per rack given that.

2) Thermal & cooling profile: the colo provided a rack_thermal_profile.png and highlighted a conservative ambient limit of 28°C at the rack inlet; thermal throttling historically kicks in for some GPU SKUs at sustained >85°C.

3) Egress shaping and peering: our networking team will enforce 5 Gbps soft egress cap per customer cross-connect during initial ramp (can burst to 8 Gbps for short windows). We also have an ISP 95th-percentile billing model.

Can your team propose a rack-level capacity plan that accounts for power/thermal caps and egress shaping and also spell out any procurement timing constraints (PDUs/cabling/approved GPU SKU lead times)? Attached are our site power profile and the colo thermal report.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Infra Lead, ACME Manufacturing
(attachment: acme_infra_specs_v2.pdf)
(attachment: site_power_profile.csv)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing question — rack power & egress constraints

Rajesh — thanks for the details and the attachments. We read the files and sketched a constrained plan with the internal folks below; a few clarifying / quick asks before we finalize numbers:

- Can you confirm the PDU distribution (single 22kW feed per rack or dual feed with 11kW legs)? That changes safe consolidation for GPUs.
- Which GPU SKU are you planning to standardize on (your spec lists two acceptable SKUs)? The modeled sustained power draw differs by ~120W/GPU between them.
- For egress shaping: is the 5 Gbps soft cap applied per cross-connect or per tenant VLAN?

Prelim thinking (high level): we will generate two rack profiles — conservative (no burst allowed, 20 kW usable) and soft-burst (allowing short 22 kW bursts, with thermal buffer). We will also model an egress-aware placement that keeps high-QPS tenants spread across bonded cross-connects to avoid 95th percentile cost spikes.

Action items:
- Rajesh: confirm PDU and chosen GPU SKU by Friday 12/10.
- Marissa/Jonas/Vanessa: I'll hand off to you to run a rack-by-rack calculaton and a short spreadsheet mapping expected QPS -> tokens/s -> egress bandwidth. Please include power draw, expected steady-state GPU utilization, and thermal margin.

I'll draft a short sizing note for procurement once we have confirmations.

— Tessa
Head of Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@acme-manufacturing.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing question — rack power & egress constraints

Thanks — ran a first-pass rack model and sharing the key tradeoffs here (will drop the spreadsheet to the Drive link once Rajesh confirms SKU and PDU). Summary:

Assumptions (conservative):
- Target GPU SKU: 4x A40-equivalent (sustained draw 300W/GPU at 80% util) — pick the SKU Rajesh confirms; model scales linearly.
- Rack usable power: 20 kW hard (22 kW burst window ~5 min, per colo)
- PUE: 1.25 (from site_power_profile.csv)
- Egress cap: 5 Gbps soft per cross-connect; assume single cross-connect unless Rajesh confirms bonded VLANs

Calculated safe consolidation (conservative):
- Platform overhead (hosts, NICs, PSU inefficiency): 2kW/rack reserved
- Remaining for GPUs: 18 kW -> at 300W/GPU => 60 GPUs per rack
- Accounting for power rails and PDUs we recommend provisioning 56 GPUs active + 4 cold spares per rack for maintenance windows (total 60 physically mounted).

Thermal & operational guardrails:
- With inlet 28°C and conservative cooling, sustained 60 GPUs at 80% pushes case temps toward 82–86°C depending on airflow. Recommend thermal margin controls: set a soft-evict threshold at 82°C and a hard throttle at 87°C. Implement a therm-triggered scale-down policy that migrates lower-priority jobs off GPUs when multiple cards reach soft-evict.

Egress mapping and QPS math (egress-aware placement):
- Typical gen-chat workload: baseline ~0.03 Gbps per 100 sustained inference QPS (encoder + decode token streams).
- For an initial target of 40k sustained QPS across the pool, estimate ~1.2 Gbps egress (spread across racks). But bursts (opensession + streaming) can raise instantaneous egress to ~3.5 Gbps.
- Recommendation: spread burst-prone tenants across at least 2 cross-connects or enable short burst windows; otherwise 95th percentile billing will penalize sustained bursts.

Autoscale recommendations:
- Start with a conservative target: 0.75x baseline packing (i.e., avoid >75% sustained GPU utilization to preserve thermal/power buffer).
- Autoscale policy: add nodes when 3-minute median GPU util >72% for 5 consecutive minutes; scale down when median <45% for 15 minutes. Include thermal signal as a hard override.

Procurement & lead times:
- If using A40-equivalent SKUs, expect 6–9 week lead time for quoted units; PDUs and redundant power distribution can add 2 weeks for procurement and cabling.
- If dual-feed PDUs are possible, final per-rack active GPU count can increase by ~10% safely.

I'll upload the spreadsheet with per-rack rows (power, predicted GPU temps at steady-state, egress bandwidth projection per tenant) to the Drive link once Rajesh confirms SKU/PDU topology.

-Marissa
Senior SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
(attachment: rack_power_worksheet_draft.xlsx - stub)

From: Rajesh Gupta <rajesh.gupta@acme-manufacturing.com>

Subject: Re: Private pool sizing question — rack power & egress constraints

Thanks Tessa/Marissa — this is very helpful. Quick confirmations:
- PDU: dual-feed available (11kW legs), so we can treat racks as dual-feed with an effective soft cap 22 kW but safer operational figure is still 20 kW unless we engage colo change window.
- GPU SKU: ACME will standardize on the A40-equivalent quoted.
- Egress: initial setup will be single cross-connect per tenant VLAN; we have the option to request a second bonded link but that requires an additional order and a 3-week lead time.

Next step: please convert the Marissa spreadsheet into a short procurement brief that lists: recommended active GPUs/rack, physical spares, PDU and cabling items and suggested lead times, recommended autoscale SLOs and the thermal thresholds we can commit to in the MSA. We will share the brief with procurement and the colo.

If you can get that to us early next week (Mon 12/13), we will start the PO routing.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Rajesh
Infra Lead, ACME Manufacturing
